procedure.step: Register your factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae) before you apply for the certificate. The factory must be outside a free zone and hold a MoIAT industrial licence and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added (a registration condition only, not your product's rule of origin). Registration takes about 3 working days. A trader can apply only for goods bought from a registered factory.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Apply through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service (eservices.moec.gov.ae or the smart app): log in, choose the service, fill in the form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (a trader also uploads the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online and submit. Processing takes about one working day. If the application is returned with comments, correct it; once approved, print the certificate.

In the application, give the HS code, description, quantity and value of the product. Each item on the certificate must qualify separately. The issuing authority may ask for detailed cost sheets or visit the factory.
Pay the certificate fee: AED 50 for an invoice value of AED 60,000 (fees run from AED 10 to AED 200 by invoice value).
Have the certificate issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. It is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import (it can list several products).

Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations there other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

Your Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, and the importer or their customs broker uploads the certificate to e-Sanchit. Under CAROTAR 2020 the importer must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed, and still has a duty of reasonable care, so you may be asked for production and cost details.

Keep your origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year in which the certificate was issued. India may ask the UAE authority to verify the certificate, and refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying the preference.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 40%' is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
The estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Minimal operations listed in Article 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never confer origin, regardless of the product-specific rule.
By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating, but the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.

Preference requires direct consignment from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

Factory registration through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism is a prerequisite for applying for a certificate of origin for India; it requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, an industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added. A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information; the exporter may be asked for production and cost details.
The exporter must keep origin records, including a cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

A certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from issue, covers one import, and must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it can be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from shipment with 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' marked.
The issuing authority may ask for detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit; each item on the certificate must qualify separately.
